scope: Follow-up of the 200 incomplete profile claims

reviews.note: The author-uploaded IUCN report lists Least Concern and publication year 2022. Its assessment date is 29 December 2021. This is not a new 2026 assessment.

reviews.claimText: Often nocturnal or hidden during daylight.
reviews.note: NParks describes generally nocturnal activity and daytime concealment in urban drains. This does not imply exclusively night activity.

reviews.claimText: Fish and other animals taken around waterways; also scavenges.
reviews.note: The feeding account supports aquatic prey and scavenging. The conservation section identifies disturbance and loss of breeding trees. Food-web position is qualitative.

reviews.claimText: A high-level predator and scavenger associated with aquatic food webs.
reviews.note: The feeding account supports aquatic prey and scavenging. The conservation section identifies disturbance and loss of breeding trees. Food-web position is qualitative.

reviews.claimText: Protecting large nesting trees and limiting disturbance helps keep suitable habitat available.
reviews.note: The feeding account supports aquatic prey and scavenging. The conservation section identifies disturbance and loss of breeding trees. Food-web position is qualitative.
ADW explicitly lists diurnal activity. The Peregrine Fund describes soaring over coastal and inland water bodies.

reviews.claimText: Follow park warnings and stay on designated paths. Keep well away from water edges, do not feed, and alert park staff to unsafe encounters.
reviews.note: AVS directs visitors to marked paths, away from water edges, and prohibits feeding. Its encounter advice includes reporting concerns to NParks.

reviews.claimText: Do not block a turtle’s route or use bright lights around nests. Observe from a distance and report nesting to NParks.
reviews.note: NParks turtle guidance supports distance, no lights, no interference and reporting nests. Keeping the route clear is conservative non-interference advice.
